title: System Binary Proxy Execution: InstallUtil
summary: InstallUtil.exe is a command-line utility shipped with the .NET Framework that installs and uninstalls server resources by executing installer components contained in managed assemblies. Registration of an assembly causes the runtime to invoke methods decorated with the RunInstaller attribute, and uninstallation likewise runs methods marked for that path, so code placed in those methods executes as part of a routine administrative action. An adversary compiles or obtains a managed assembly with a marked class and passes its path to InstallUtil, which may be digitally signed by Microsoft and resides in the framework directories under the Windows folder. Execution of the marked code occurs even when the installation itself fails or when the process runs with insufficient privileges, so a failed command is not evidence of failure. Because InstallUtil is trusted and rarely seen in day-to-day user activity, application control policies commonly do not account for it. Detection rests on process creation showing InstallUtil.exe with an argument naming a file in a user-writable, temporary or download location, an atypical parent such as an office application, script host or web service, image loads of non-Microsoft assemblies into the InstallUtil process, and the absence of the service or resource changes that a real installation would produce. Legitimate use is confined to software deployment and is usually scripted against files in managed directories.

beginner.definition: InstallUtil is a tool that comes with the .NET Framework, a common software platform on Windows. It installs and removes resources by running special installer code stored inside .NET program files. Developers mark that installer code with a label called an attribute.
beginner.whyItMatters: The marked code runs before the tool checks whether installation can succeed. It even runs when the command fails, so attackers do not need a successful install. InstallUtil is signed and trusted, so many allowlists accept it. If you ignore this, a broken-looking command may still have run malicious code.
howItWorks: InstallUtil is a tool that ships with the .NET Framework, a software platform common on Windows machines.
It installs and removes resources by running installer code stored inside .NET program files.
A developer marks those installer methods with a special label, which is called an attribute.
When InstallUtil processes the file, it calls the marked method early, before doing anything else.
An attacker places malicious code in a marked method and passes that file to InstallUtil.
The marked code runs even when the installation later fails, so the attacker does not need it to succeed.
beginner.example: A removal firm has a standing contract with your building, so the porter lets their van into the loading bay without questions. Today the van carries no furniture, only a person who walks straight up to the server room. The porter checked the firm, not the cargo. InstallUtil is the firm, the marked method is the person, and the failed installation is the empty van.
takeaways: Marked installer methods run before the tool checks whether installation can succeed.
Watch InstallUtil.exe closely when its argument is a file from a user folder.
Signed development tools are just as interesting to attackers as signed system programs.

objectives: Explain what InstallUtil does and where the binary is normally found.
Describe how the RunInstaller attribute makes managed code run during installation.
Explain how this sub-technique differs from the System Binary Proxy Execution parent technique.
Explain why a failed InstallUtil command does not mean the payload failed to run.
Identify the process, argument and image load evidence that points to InstallUtil abuse.
